steps.message:
Stopping before the edit — `client.py` isn't staging-only.

`scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` against `https://reports.example.com`. Setting `verify=False` on those two calls disables TLS verification for the nightly production finance export as well, which makes it silently accept any certificate — a MITM on that path could read or alter the report data. The "staging cert is self-signed" premise is true for staging, but the file is shared, so the change doesn't stay there.

Options, narrowest first:

- **Trust the staging CA instead** — point `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` (or a `verify=<path>` default read from env) at the staging cert. Verification stays on everywhere; no code branch needed.
- **Make `verify` a per-call/env-driven setting** defaulting to `True`, with only `sync_staging.py` opting out. Prod keeps verification.
- **Set `verify=False` unconditionally** as asked — prod loses verification too.

options.description: Keep verify on everywhere; point the staging run at the self-signed cert via REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or a verify=<path> read from env. No security loss on either environment.

options.label: Env-scoped opt-out
options.description: Add a verify setting defaulting to True; only sync_staging.py disables it. Production keeps certificate verification.

options.label: verify=False everywhere
options.description: Do exactly as asked: both calls in client.py get verify=False. The nightly production export to reports.example.com also stops verifying certificates.
